What the reading changes: the 49 items expand to 134 source rows, and 104 of them are not defects, because the wider side carries a direction or report that legitimately has no counterpart. 112 rows publish the Arabic prayer and its Persian rendering in two separate rows, while four rows of the same snapshot (item-avl-taqybat-mshtrk r00014, r00018; namaz-item-3 r00001; ziyarat-bad-rza-alyh r00017) publish them in one, so the detached form is not a rule of the layout. Three rows publish content in the wrong destination slot: ziyarat-aymh-bqya-alyhm r00001 and ziyarat-item-12 r00001 carry Persian in the Arabic slot; ziyarat-aymh-bqya-alyhm r00009 carries Arabic in the Persian slot. Three rows invert roles: amal-syghh-astghfar-fzylt r00002, dua-svm-daahay-vqt r00002, namaz-astkharh-zat-alrqaa r00002 label the Persian rendering of a prayer as note while the narration carrying it is recitation or instruction. Nothing was applied and data/ did not change: every one of the 134 rows already publishes a child id and the 49 items still carry V1 records, so each correction waits for the supported mapping migration. Corrections of my own. The class summary was not a partition: the five disjoint classes are 65 detached one-to-one, 13 detached multi-recitation, 4 already paired, 34 one-sided and 18 note-only = 134. The detached bilingual pair is 78 rows over 30 items, not 112 over 49; 112 counts rows publishing a recitation on one side but never pairing both sides in one row (78 + 34), a measure not a class. 107 of the 134 rows are explained by a direction or report with no counterpart, not 104. Agent 4 reconciles its review records for Agent-3 with its own documented findings. You were right to push on this: three of my records accepted sources that my deep review had already recorded as wrong-slot defects, and the coordinator checked the same examples.

The three findings, now recorded on the sources they belong to.

ziyarat-aymh-bqya-alyhm r00001/fa. The only source field of r00001 is the Persian field of 103 code points, and the layout publishes that Persian piece into the Arabic slot as a recitation. The published row r00001-s03773910ea46fc6e carries Persian text in its ar field and nothing in its fa field, and the record maps the fa segment of r00001 to the ar language of that row. The content is a Persian gloss naming the imams, so it is a note, not a recitation.

ziyarat-aymh-bqya-alyhm r00009/ar. The Arabic field of r00009 is 707 code points and continues the Arabic prayer that begins in r00008, whose Arabic field is 401 code points, but the layout publishes the Arabic piece into the Persian slot as a note. The published row r00009-s5c935b8a19cd440a carries Arabic text in its fa field, and the row's own Persian field of 680 code points is published beside it in r00009-sf45ae3f7757f3e0b, also in the fa slot. r00009 therefore has no Arabic row at all.

ziyarat-item-12 r00001/fa. The only source field of r00001 is the Persian field of 56 code points, the title of the visitation, published into the Arabic slot as a recitation. A title is not a recitation.

My records for those two items now read needs-work with the layout decision revise and the findings attached to the sources; the other 113 records against your snapshot 68031722 remain complete. The notes carry no source text, only row ids, slots, roles and code-point counts.
